answer: Enrollment happens once, in person, and every check is chosen to make a copy useless. A camera must catch the applicant's pulse in capillary motion, the ivory sclera of one eye brightening under a light, and a yarrow pollen skin prick whose flare starts on a schedule no one can rehearse. Those signals fuse into a one-way code, so a second registration from the same body collides in the index and is refused, while a synthesized face never produces the flare. A k-seat farm needs k real, willing people at k appointments, and each body buys exactly one seat.
